leave_bereavement_days_007.evidence: The employee shall be granted bereavement leave of absence with pay and without loss of Paid Time Off (PTO) benefits for up to a maximum of three (3) regularly scheduled days within a two (2) week period.

leave_bereavement_relatives_008.answer: Child, spouse/domestic partner, parent, grandparent, sibling, grandchild, or anyone of the same relationship by marriage. Close non-family members covered via case-by-case analysis.
leave_bereavement_relatives_008.evidence: “Immediate family member” is defined as a child, spouse/domestic partner, parent, grandparent, sibling, grandchild, or anyone of the same relationship by marriage.
leave_bereavement_relatives_008.coder_notes: Updated page number from 42 to 41, as the definition appears under Section E on page 41.

leave_parental_paid_009.evidence: Every parent who takes leave pursuant to the Family Medical Leave Act provisions regarding the birth or adoption of their child is eligible for paid leave during the first two weeks of FMLA. Parental leave shall not be counted against PTO and holidays.

leave_pregnancy_disability_010.evidence: Leave without pay for up to twelve (12) months may be granted to members of the bargaining units to provide extended care for a child following the termination of maternity leave, adoption, or for long-term illnesses of children.

leave_adoption_childcare_011.evidence: Leave without pay for up to twelve (12) months may be granted to members of the bargaining units to provide extended care for a child following the termination of maternity leave, adoption, or for long-term illnesses of children.

leave_fmla_012.evidence: An employee who has used up all current and accumulated days of PTO allowance, and who has used up all leave available pursuant to the Family Medical Leave Act... may be placed by administrative action on extended health leave
